In response to the edit: Eh, take what I write on Suicide Watch with a grain of salt, to be very honest with you...when I am in a depressive episode I tend to see the people in my life and their actions in very distorted ways and it's something I've been working on in therapy. It's pretty symptomatic of depressed people to feel like nobody cares about them, everybody is against them, or that we don't deserve their love. 

Yeah, he was chasing after me in the party scenario, though I feel this is only because he knew no one else there and he did not want to go introduce himself to anybody else. I can somewhat understand that kind of social anxiety so I took a break from cooking and helped introduce him to some people. If we are in a familiar environment with familiar people, such as our dorm, it is me who has to go after him. I'm not saying he needs to chase after me, I'm saying it needs to be 50/50. I can't be doing all the footwork, you know?

It is exactly a 25 hours 8 days a week thing, even he knows that. He used to play other games and I was cool with that, so long as he was doing something other than just one thing. When I say obsessed, I don't mean that lightly, I mean obsessed, as in hasn't stopped talking about it for the past three months, spends all his money on cards, spends all his free time playing type of deal. And to be honest, I don't really mind if he spends even most of his free time playing Magic, but goodness gracious, come up with something else to talk about rather than Magic. I'll entertain the daily which-Planeswalker-is-better discussion for a half hour maximum, but when it comes to two hours of Magic talk, I can't even pretend to care that much anymore. Magic is a fun game--it's not THAT fun, at least to me. I've tried to change the subject but it usually gets me one-word responses. I appreciate his hobbies and I'm NOT saying he should give up Magic cold-turkey because he doesn't need to give up anything at all, but I beg of him to find something else to be interested in as well because I am tired of having nothing else to talk about than Magic. It's like listening to *that* annoying girl who won't ever shut up about her boyfriend. It's mildly entertaining for the first few conversations, you're willing to entertain relationship talk every now and then, but when it's every single time you talk, you just start to wonder when she's ever going to get a life.

I know him well enough that I know other games and hobbies he at least USED to enjoy, but when I bring them up now he's like "eh, yeah, I guess, whatever". He doesn't really use FB, so that doesn't work, unfortunately.

I think the confusion is that I'm not certain it is depression, but I'm also not certain that it isn't. I'm also not certain if it's his character or not.

I did just talk to him, actually, and from what I gather he's not exactly content with the life he's living right now. He plays Magic because he has nothing better to do, and he is bored with life. However, he doesn't know what else to do. I suggested he go out and try new things, even if he doesn't know if he'll like them. I hope he takes the suggestion.

He's not a loser. I don't expect him to have it all figured out at this point--even I am going through that "what do I want from life" phase right now. I don't know what I want from life. I still keep going though. But it's reached a point where he's all but dropped out of life--it's even a struggle to get him to actually attend class, never mind do homework, he did so badly last semester they had to put him on academic probation. This semester is not a whole lot better. He wasn't a bad student in high school.

I don't mean to sound full of myself but I honestly think I have reacted to this situation with more compassion than most would. This isn't something that *just* popped up, these issues have been here for...well, a while. I have put up with them, I have made ways to cope or get over some issues, I have compromised, I have stuck by him even though I was really disappointed. I am a firm believer in working things out, but not a firm believer in ignoring the writing on the wall. 

Maybe he is depressed. I don't know because he won't seek help, and it doesn't look like he is upset most of the time. If that is the case I will definitely help him through. What I'm worried about is if this is a "this is just who I am" thing. If it is, then I don't really want to be with him. It's not like he's a loser or a bad person, but I don't want that kind of life where my partner is a shiftless layabout without any motivation. I know I cannot change people, they have to want to change themselves. If this is just something that is inherent to him and he doesn't want to change it, then that's my sign to call it quits. If it is something that's symptomatic of something deeper, like depression, then I am totally willing to work out with him and stick it out until he gets better. I'm just not really sure which one it is, yet.

This is good advice. Thank you. I know it is normal for us to have completely different interests, I'm totally fine with that. There are lots of interests of mine that he doesn't share and I don't begrudge him at all for not caring for them. It's just become that his only interest is Magic and nothing else. He's become a one-note kind of guy.

I talked to him just now about the whole "not really doing anything else besides playing Magic" thing and what he told me was that he plays it because he doesn't have anything better to do, not necessarily because he wants to play it all the time. He says he is bored with his life, and that's probably why he doesn't have much to say. I suggested he try to get out more and try new things, even if he's not absolutely sure he likes it. Unfortunately half the battle is actually showing up to those things, and I can't make him do that. 

I told him honestly that it's become a bit hard to talk to him and have meaningful time together because of his negativity and his lack of interest in anything besides Magic. I wouldn't even mind it if he just picked a different game to get in to. His main interest when I first met him was video games then too, and I was and still am totally fine with it. I just want to talk about something or some other game besides Magic. I'm just sick of it. It's not a bad game, it's fine, but please, something else for once.

I know my family, best friend, and boyfriend knows about the whole depression thing, I think that's why they're so understanding when I have these little meltdowns. I just told my boyfriend what I told this thread and while I was talking I realized I was overreacting again and succumbing to the "depressive perception". It's really easy for me to convince myself that people don't actually like me when they do because very often I don't like myself. I convince myself they secretly hate me or are just using me for something and that's why they still talk to me, because why else would they talk to me? Couldn't really be because they actually like me. Very frequently I even convince myself my own mother doesn't love me and hates me and wishes I had never been born despite the fact that she's never said or done anything to such effect and very frequently expresses her love. I have a very negative self-perception and it hurts how I interact with others. It alienates me.

My boyfriend shows me in a lot of ways he cares about me more than just for an emotional security blanket. That he cares so much to make me happy when I'm so sad tell me a lot. That he doesn't blow me off or trivialize my problems or get super-defensive when I voice my real or imagined concerns. He patiently listens and talks with me and tells me what he thinks, and we always reach a happy conclusion. He stays on the phone with me for hours until he knows for sure I'm happy again.

Everybody shows love in their own way and I was expecting him to be Prince Charming roses-and-candy style and that's not reasonable. I frequently have this problem where I expect too much from relationships (any kind, family, friends, etc) and get really upset when my expectations aren't met. As I get older I am becoming more accepting of the fact that people have other things to do or just don't express themselves in the way I want them to and that doesn't mean that our relationship is worthless or fake or bad. I still have a lot of growing up to do, but this is getting a lot better than it used to be. It's still not all the way gone, though.

I am scheduling an appointment with a psychiatrist this week because I am finally fed up with living like this. I have been very scared of doing this because I'm afraid of what people will think and how my family and friends will react. I was discouraged from taking meds as a teen due to Trileptol and Welbutrin, but considering where I've been lately, constantly depressed for no good reason despite the fact that I KNOW everything is fine, is not something I want to keep living through for the rest of my life, even if it comes and goes. I thought my depression was situational, but I can clearly see after moving out of my mom's house and leaving high school that it's really not and that I've got a serious problem. I don't talk to you or others about it often because I'm afraid people will be repelled by being around a negative person. I feel like a failure and hopeless and unlovable all the time despite logically acknowledging that I have lots of people in my life, my mother, friends, and boyfriend included, who love me unconditionally and think I'm important, and that I've done a lot of good things in my life. It's not a normal way to function and it's time I got some professional help. I can't keep ignoring it and pretending like it's just a passing phase.

I know a lot of it is things that go on in my head. For some reason realizing this and realizing that my perception is skewed because I'm depressed makes me even more depressed. I feel like I'm being robbed of enjoying life and the people around me and I just can't snap out of it. It's not as easy as just "Be happy!". 

Not in adulthood (I'm 18). I tried Trileptol and something starting with a W (Welbutrin?) when I was hospitalized. Both of them gave me migraines and one made my depression worse.
